title: Five Million Slaughterhouse Brains — Geoffrey Harris's Mocked 1948 Portal-Vessel Hypothesis, the 21-Year Guillemin vs. Schally 'Nobel Duel' Processing >5 Million Sheep & Pig Hypothalami for 1 mg TRH (1969), GnRH (1971) & Somatostatin (1973), Rosalyn Yalow's RIA (1977 Nobel), Leuprolide, Elagolix & Octreotide Inside Human GnRHR, TRHR & SSTR2 (PDB 7BR3, 7XW9, 7T10, 7T11)

teenKit.tldr: To isolate just one milligram of brain chemicals that control our hormones, two rival scientists had to process over five million animal brains in industrial slaughterhouse blenders. Their cutthroat 21-year feud birthed modern endocrinology and life-saving drugs used today.
teenKit.whyItMatters: The brutal competition behind these discoveries gave us the exact molecular treatments we use today for prostate cancer, endometriosis, and fertility struggles.
keyTakeaways: Geoffrey Harris was initially mocked for arguing that the brain (not individual glands) is the ultimate master control center of the body's hormones.
The 21-year Nobel duel between Roger Guillemin and Andrew Schally involved processing millions of sheep and pig hypothalami in freezing, vinegar-soaked laboratories.
Modern atomic-level structural biology allows us to map exactly how drugs like Leuprolide and Elagolix fit into human cellular receptors like microscopic locks and keys.

vocab.meaning: The command center region of the brain that links the nervous system to the endocrine system by releasing master control hormones.
The once-mocked idea that the brain controls the pituitary gland by releasing chemical messengers directly into a specialized network of blood vessels.
A breakthrough technique invented by Rosalyn Yalow that uses radioactive isotopes to measure microscopic quantities of hormones in the blood.
A specialized protein molecule on a cell surface that binds to specific chemical messengers to trigger a physiological response.

quiz.question: What extreme industrial process did Guillemin and Schally use to extract tiny amounts of hypothalamic hormones?
options: Synthesizing them entirely from synthetic plastics in a clean room
Blending over five million sheep and pig brains in industrial meat-packing facilities
Extracting them safely from plant roots using high-temperature steam
Harvesting them from voluntary human plasma donations
quiz.explanation: They had to process millions of animal brains in industrial blenders just to isolate a single milligram of pure TRH.

quiz.question: What was the main revolutionary idea proposed by Geoffrey Harris in the 1950s that initial textbooks mocked?
options: The stomach controls all human emotions.
The brain controls the pituitary gland via chemical portal vessels.
Glands function completely independently of the nervous system.
Hormones are actually electrical signals traveling down bones.
quiz.explanation: Harris argued that the brain uses specialized blood vessels to talk directly to the pituitary gland, a concept initially met with deep skepticism.

quiz.question: Who was the Bronx-born nuclear physicist who revolutionized endocrinology by inventing Radioimmunoassay (RIA), winning a Nobel Prize?
quiz.explanation: Rosalyn Yalow co-developed RIA, allowing scientists to track minute concentrations of hormones in the blood for the very first time.
